paragraphs: Rav Yitzchak bar Ada, or the son of Rav Ada.

In [Chullin 15b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.15b.3): “Rabbi Yitzchak bar Ada said: Rav said.” In [Berakhot 4a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.4a): “Rav Yitzchak bar Ada said”—and some say, Rav Yitzchak son of Rav Ada—“What is the verse?” etc. In [Eruvin 20b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.20b) he said, “The partitions were not permitted…” etc. In Midrash Tehillim, chapter 92, section 11: “R' Yitzchak bar Ada said: Just as a date palm’s shade is far from it, so the reward of the righteous is far from them, until the World to Come, as it is stated…” etc.[^1][^2]

notes.text: אר״י, ארי״בא and רי״בא are resolved contextually as forms of Yitzchak bar Ada’s name, rather than turned into invented names such as Ari-biba; their titles are checked separately at each occurrence. The alternative bar Ada/son of Rav Ada wording remains distinct. לא הותרו is retained as a negative opening, “were not permitted…,” without supplying the missing condition. לע״הב is the ordinary World to Come. The printed פ״צב־יא is a locator within Midrash Tehillim, not a new claim that the quotation is the biblical verse Psalm 92:11. The Bavli טו:, ד. and כ: conventionally give 15b, 4a and 20b. The complete matching passages have now been checked in the named digital editions.

Hyman’s full Rav in the heading and the full alternative ‘Rav Yitzchak son of Rav Ada’ are preserved. Davidson’s exact Chullin passage explicitly has Rabbi Yitzchak bar Ada reporting Rav, so that abbreviated occurrence is rendered Rabbi. Its Berakhot passage has Rav Yitzchak bar Ada, but the alternative is ‘son of Rav Idi,’ not Hyman’s ‘son of Rav Ada’; Hyman’s wording is retained with the difference disclosed. The Eruvin passage explicitly has Rabbi Yitzchak bar Ada; the translation’s ‘he said’ does not transfer the heading’s Rav into that quotation. The OYW Midrash Tehillim text has only the abbreviated ר' יצחק בר אדא, so its occurrence remains R'. The palm saying is at [92:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Midrash_Tehillim.92.8) in that digital text rather than Hyman’s cited section 11. The different titles, parentage readings and section numbering have not been harmonized, and no historical identity is established.
